vulnerability_analysis: The Allin token contract has owner-controlled fee settings that can be abused. The owner can call setFeeReceivers() to redirect marketing fees to any address, and setFees() to set excessive fee percentages (up to 100%). During swapBack(), collected fees are converted to BNB and sent to the marketingFeeReceiver. This allows an attacker with owner privileges to drain BNB from user transactions.
attack_strategy: 1. Impersonate the contract owner to gain authorized access. 2. Set marketingFeeReceiver to attacker address. 3. Set excessive marketing fee (90%+). 4. Enable trading. 5. Inject tokens into contract to trigger swapBack threshold. 6. Execute a token transfer to accumulate fees. 7. Trigger swapBack() which converts fees to BNB and sends to attacker.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Use vm.startPrank() to impersonate owner (0x4CE6D95Ba0f6CBEa8CdC43E1a77359E609bC730C from constructor). 2. Call setFeeReceivers() with attacker as marketingFeeReceiver. 3. Call setFees() with 9000 marketing fee and 10000 denominator (90% fee). 4. Call tradingStatus(true) to enable trading. 5. Use deal() to inject tokens into contract to meet swapThreshold. 6. Transfer tokens from attacker to trigger fee collection and swapBack. 7. Attacker receives BNB from marketing fees.
